clue.text: Old book's identifying effective lifetime of controversial project?

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: of puts the lifetime after the project's name, the day belonging to the Dome

parts.note: the Millennium Dome in London was a much-criticised project, here in the possessive, the Dome's
the Dome was open as an attraction only for the year 2000, so its day was its working life

explanation.surface: A question about an ancient record that reveals how long a disputed scheme really lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome, a British exhibition building, was open to the public only through the year 2000: its day. The Domesday Book is England's survey of 1086.
explanation.definitionFit: The Domesday Book is William the Conqueror's 1086 survey of England, a famously ancient record.

clue.text: Complete boiling down process in two short months

parts.note: December is abbreviated to Dec
October is abbreviated to Oct

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction says the reduction will take a couple of months.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to extract a substance's essence by boiling it down.

clue.text: Dodgy dealing — firm given 500 up front

indicators.note: up front says the sum comes before the firm in the answer

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
a firm is a company or commercial concern

explanation.surface: A shady deal in which a company is handed five hundred pounds in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given 500 up front' reads as a bribe, but 'up front' places the slang for £500 first.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for underhand or mischievous behaviour, trickery.

clue.text: Groans, struggling into exotic garment

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of the word groans writhing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone groans as they wrestle their way into an unfamiliar foreign wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South-East Asia and the Pacific.

clue.text: Trying to find rooms later

parts.note: to be after something is to be seeking it
wards are rooms in a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone house-hunting will look for accommodation at a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards is an adverb meaning at a later time, subsequently.

clue.text: Took steps to be in time

definitions.text: Took steps to be in time

parts.words: Took steps to be in time
parts.note: reads as taking action to avoid lateness, but describes moving the feet in rhythm to music

explanation.surface: Someone acted promptly so as not to be late.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing is stepping rhythmically in time with music.

clue.text: Delightful fresh bread-loaves half gone?

indicators.note: fresh signals a new version of the letters, here bread together with a cut-down loaves
half gone means only the first half of the word loaves is kept

explanation.surface: A baker's question whether fresh loaves that have half sold out are a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half gone' keeps LOA, the first half of LOAVES; 'fresh' rearranges BREAD with LOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming, lovable, a delight.

clue.text: One's right to restrain criminal activity

definitions.text: One's right to restrain criminal activity

parts.words: One's right to restrain criminal activity
parts.note: describes the power an ordinary member of the public has to detain someone seen committing a crime

explanation.surface: A statement of the individual's entitlement to stop wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: In British law a private person may detain someone caught committing an offence, a power named after ordinary members of the public.

clue.text: Thinking of an afternoon doze?

parts.note: a reverie is literally what one might see dozing in the daytime, and also idle musing

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a nap after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie or fanciful thought while awake, which is literally a vision had during the day.

clue.text: Reset correct type, one verse needing unusual layout

indicators.note: reset is a printer's word for setting type again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A typesetter is told to redo the type, since one poem needs a strange arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reset' rearranges the fourteen letters of CORRECT, TYPE and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete poetry arranges its words on the page into a visual shape, so its layout is part of its meaning.

clue.text: See 9
Do they take you for a tidy sum?

definitions.text: Do they take you for a tidy sum?

parts.words: Do they take you for a tidy sum?
parts.note: the idiom to take someone to the ... means to fleece them, while a tidy sum is a lot of money and tidy also hints at cleaning

explanation.surface: A suspicion that someone is overcharging.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-cleaning shops clean clothes, and being taken to them is the idiom for being swindled.

clue.text: Some chap at zero in chess tournament — he's no good

definitions.text: in chess tournament — he's no good

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A player who has scored nothing in a chess event is clearly no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A patzer is chess slang for a weak, inept player.

clue.text: Did you force that woman slurring to have peculiar drink?

indicators.note: slurring means the words are run together carelessly in speech, giving the sound of a Caribbean island

parts.note: did you force her is did you make her, slurred to something like d'ya make 'er
rum is a British word for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: An accusatory question to a drunk, slurring speaker about forcing a woman to take a strange drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did you make her' slurred becomes 'd'ya make 'er', which sounds like the island name; 'to have' links it to RUM, peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica rum is a dark, heavy rum distilled in Jamaica.

clue.text: Sam recalled passing time in this port

definitions.text: Sam recalled passing time in this port

parts.words: Sam recalled passing time in this port
parts.note: in a famous 1942 film the pianist Sam is asked to play a song about time going by, and the film is named after a Moroccan port

explanation.surface: Someone called Sam remembers whiling away hours in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film, Sam is asked to play 'As Time Goes By', so 'passing time' is the song, not idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan Atlantic port gives its name to the film in which Sam plays that song.

clue.text: Since sign of disapproval, see how to apply sagacity

parts.note: as can mean since, because
tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with one

explanation.surface: Advice on using wisdom since someone has tutted.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's seat; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is the usual crossword see.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something astutely means doing it with shrewdness and wisdom.

clue.text: See 2
Very loyal? So you said twice, in high-pitched voice

annotationWithheld.why: Very loyal? So you said twice, in high-pitched voice (4-4): no parse found for BLUE; 'so you said' may give TRUE but nothing in 'twice, in high-pitched voice' supplies BLUE, so the clue may be misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Very loyal? So you said twice, in high-pitched voice

clue.text: Paid for ale drunk-a fair bargain

parts.note: to square a debt is to settle or pay it

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word ale staggering out of order

explanation.surface: Someone settled the bill for some beer they drank, and it was a good deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A square deal is an honest, fair transaction.

clue.text: Beginning to count punches

explanation.surface: Starting a count, or describing a boxer's combination.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting begins with the first two numbers, and in boxing a jab followed by a cross is a classic combination.

clue.text: See 7
Old boy perhaps leaving a lasting impression?

explanation.surface: A former pupil who makes a memorable mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdated old person is called a relic, and a preserved imprint of ancient life in rock is a lasting mark.

clue.text: Reduced educational facilities, formerly for both men and women

parts.note: unis is the shortened form of universities
ex means former, as in an ex-wife

explanation.surface: Colleges with cut budgets that used to be single-sex now admit both.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex describes something suitable for either sex, such as a haircut or a toilet.

clue.text: Race is on to thrash out plot's outline

indicators.note: to thrash out is to work something over vigorously, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A deadline looms, and the writers must hammer out the story's summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay synopsis or sketch of a story's plot.

clue.text: They harmonise with skill-classless members of union

indicators.note: classless means the abbreviation for class, CL, is removed

parts.note: to do something cleverly is to do it skilfully
trade union members address each other as brother

explanation.surface: A tuneful group praised for both skill and egalitarian union membership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classless' drops CL (class) from CLEVERLY, leaving EVERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The American duo Don and Phil sang in famously close two-part harmony.

clue.text: See 24
They'll give you the creeps

parts.note: creeps are sycophants, and people who always agree with you surround you with them

explanation.surface: A warning about something unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who agree with everything a boss says are toadies, or creeps.

clue.text: Godlike individual's inaccurate self-assessment?

parts.note: a deity describing itself as a mere human who will die would be wrong, so the words split as I'm plus a word for subject to death

explanation.surface: A god wrongly sizing itself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathless being, such as a god, lives for ever.
